thread:
incident-bot: [PAGING] GPU fleet: elevated Xid/driver-reset rate detected in us-west-2-gpu-pool. Auto-alert threshold breached (5m). Suspected cascade on subset of A100 hosts. Paging @anya_oncall and @mike_sre :rotating_light:

anya_oncall: Got it, joining. Watching metrics now.

mike_sre: I'm online. grabbing telemetry from the affected hosts.

incident-bot: Autosnapshot: 5743210987. Affected hosts: gpu-node-22, gpu-node-24, gpu-node-27 (partial). Error sample: "Xid 79: GPU has fallen off the bus" (driver).

anya_oncall: First check: any recent driver rollouts or kernel updates?

mike_sre: No rollout in last 24h. Kernel tags unchanged. I see a soft spike in ECC correctable errors on node-24 prior to resets. attaching quick log snip: ```nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,index,driver_model.current,compute_mode,pstate --format=csv -l 1``` returned repeating XID lines and rapid dfatal stack logs.

carol_prod: Any customer-facing errors? Prod logs show a handful of 5xxs for /v1/generate during the 09:12-09:18 window for a subset of requests pinned to us-west-2. About ~70 requests failed, latency rose for others.

dave_support: I already saw two customer tickets tied to time window. Marking P0 if it’s ongoing.

anya_oncall: Ok plan: 1) Isolate the noisy nodes from scheduling, 2) Evacuate pods with graceful drain, 3) Apply driver reload on node and monitor. If resets persist, cordon + reboot.

mike_sre: Running drain on gpu-node-24: `kubectl drain gpu-node-24 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60`

infra-bot: Drain event recorded: evicting 18 pods from gpu-node-24. ETA ~2m.

anya_oncall: Started canary fallback: routing ~10% of traffic away from us-west-2 to us-east-1 for gen endpoints. This should reduce customer impact.

mike_sre: After drain, I attempted `sudo modprobe -r nvidia_uvm nvidia` then `modprobe nvidia nvidia_uvm`. Driver reload succeeded on gpu-node-24 but Xid spikes resumed within ~3 minutes.

carol_prod: Noted — latency blip again around 09:26, some timeouts. Customers on heavy-batched inference affected more.

mike_sre: Node-22 shows increasing KVM I/O errors and badge of ECC correctables climbing. Running `nvidia-bug-report.sh` to capture full traces and GPU dmesg.

anya_oncall: We should escalate fleet-level mitigation. @infra-bot, can you schedule an immediate node pool warm-replace for the remaining A100 hosts in that rack? Prefer to rotate to spare capacity and reduce pack density.

infra-bot: Warm-replace job queued for rack-r4-usw2, priority high. Expected node swap within 12 minutes.

dave_support: Sending templated update to affected customers: "We are investigating GPU driver resets in us-west-2. We're routing traffic to alternate regions and will follow up."

mike_sre: For traceability, here's the exact Xid excerpt from /var/log/syslog on gpu-node-27: `kernel: NVRM: Xid (0000007c): 79, 0, 0x0c04a3b4` — similar to previous noisy-reset incidents but without a full kernel panic.

anya_oncall: Given repeated modprobe reload failing, we should cordon the remaining noisy nodes to avoid cascading schedule-induced flaps. I'll cordon node-22 and node-27.

mike_sre: Commands: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-22` -> Done. `kubectl cordon gpu-node-27` -> Done. Starting controlled reboots for both after snapshotting metrics.

carol_prod: Customer count impacted: 3 active customers had degraded responses. SLO hit estimated at 0.6% for the 15m window. Logging a customer impact note in the incident tracker.

anya_oncall: Escalation: alerting hardware team to run onsite diagnostics for rack-r4-usw2. Assigning to @mike_sre for remote triage and to hardware ops for physical checks.

mike_sre: Reboots completed for 22 and 27. Post-reboot, node-22: driver loaded cleanly, no Xid observed in 7m; node-27: Xid resumed after ~2m. Taking node-27 out of rotation and leaving cordon.

infra-bot: Node replacement initiated for gpu-node-27. New host provisioning in progress.

carol_prod: Push a status update to status.redwood.ai: "Partial GPU instability in us-west-2 impacting small percentage of generation requests. Traffic routing applied; mitigation in progress."

dave_support: Customer update sent. Two customers replied asking for ETA; provided tentative timeline ~45-60m for full normalization.

anya_oncall: Mike, capture final telemetry and upload to the incident ticket (include `nvidia-bug-report` and kernel dmesg). Also add the runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-driver-resets

mike_sre: Uploaded artifacts to ticket #INC-5743. Quick diff: ECC correctables were 10x baseline on node-24 and node-27 prior to resets. Suggest hardware swap for those GPUs.

carol_prod: Moving to customer-impact review: create a follow-up postmortem focused on kernel-driver interactions and early ECC detection thresholds.

anya_oncall: Handoff: I'm going offline in ~30m. @mike_sre you have oncall ownership after me. Mike, ensure the replacement node is healthy and monitor for 2h before clear.

mike_sre: Acknowledged. I'll own the follow-up. Current state: us-west-2 traffic partially routed away, node-24 reprovisioned healthy, node-22 healthy, node-27 replaced. Continuing monitoring.

infra-bot: Incident state updated: mitigation in progress -> partial-mitigated.

anya_oncall: Thanks team. We'll reconvene if Xid reappears. Final note: add metric alert tuning to detect ECC correctable slope rather than absolute count to catch regressions earlier. :white_check_mark:

mike_sre: Noted, adding to action items in the ticket. Closing active paging thread.
